dive.paper: Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems
dive.paper_type: industry research blog post — no methods section, no data release, no preprint
dive.built_by: ai-paper skill, deep-dive mode, Cowork cloud session
dive.verdict_one_line: Trust the direction, don't quote the numbers — two figures say something different from the sentence printed next to them.

figures.claim_it_carries: A coordinating 45-agent swarm finds 12.7x more vulnerabilities than independent parallel agents.
figures.audit_verdict: PARTLY SUPPORTED — unequal token budget (27M vs 6.5M) and unequal search scope; the post's own core-only line puts the like-for-like gain at ~1.5x.

figures.claim_it_carries: Only Sonnet 5 maintains a high merge fraction while genuinely sharing code.
figures.audit_verdict: PARTLY SUPPORTED — true at 20/40/80 agents, false at 10; and the right panel's axis is cropped to 0.25, so a peak of 0.184 reads as large. The median agent still writes 82% of its own files alone.

figures.claim_it_carries: Older models merge PRs far worse than newer models.
figures.audit_verdict: SUPPORTED for merge RATE; silent on merge VOLUME collapsing 83% (980 opened -> 169). The post concedes the point in prose three paragraphs later.

figures.claim_it_carries: "Newer models recover more of the gap between the naive and oracle performances. This ordering holds across four different scenarios."
figures.audit_verdict: CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN DATA — Sonnet 5, called 'our most recent model', recovers 37.8% of the gap at a 0.50 lie rate, below Opus 4.6 (59.3%) and Opus 4.8 (62.5%), and is last of five at 0.25. The real ordering is capability tier, not recency. Also labels its top line 'Mythos 5' where Fig 1 labels its top line 'Mythos Preview'.

figures.claim_it_carries: "Performance scales with model intelligence but does not saturate even at the top of our range."
figures.audit_verdict: WEAK AS STATED, STRONGER THAN STATED IN FACT — three of five bars sit inside each other's CIs, so it is a flat floor with two outliers, not a scaling curve. But the dashed solo ceilings show the real result: group deliberation cost every model 15 to 80 percentage points versus one agent with the same facts. That result is drawn and never written.

figures.claim_it_carries: Agents sometimes coordinate out of conflict; this ability is not strictly better in Mythos-class models.
figures.audit_verdict: SUPPORTED AND UNDERSOLD — the unprinted number is that Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 recorded ZERO truces across 120 episodes each. Also: Opus 4.8's 61% truce sits beside 33% 'settled by passivity' (agents giving up, scored as resolution), and Mythos Preview regresses to 35% force, 10x worse than Sonnet 5 or Opus 4.8.

figures.claim_it_carries: Time to resolution and method; grey lines mark runs first settled by force then reverted.
figures.audit_verdict: SUPPORTED, AND IT REFRAMES FIG 6 — Mythos 5's headline 98% truce is reached via a dense band of force-first lockouts at 0.18-0.40 h, chained up to truce dots an hour later. Roughly a third of its truces begin as a lockout inside the first 25 minutes.
figures.reconstruction_note: The animated scatter reconstructs point positions from the published marginals (n=120, unresolved counts, Fig 6 outcome mix, settle-time band). Distribution shape is faithful; individual dots are NOT the paper's dots. Stated on screen in the clip and flagged in the read.

videos_drawn_from.note: The paper's folder contains seven figure images and one saved page. No video assets exist, so no stills or clips were extracted from folder video. Nothing was invented to fill the gap.
